goal: Lets an interrupted -reindex resume from where it left off instead of restarting at blk00000.dat
Aims to save node operators from redoing hours of reindex work after a power loss or manual interrupt
reviewability: Paused: author switched the PR to draft to gather real-world measurements before continuing
Review would be premature until the author confirms the approach actually helps
agreement: Disputed: maflcko questions whether the change improves anything once you correctly drop -reindex on restart (maflcko)
mzumsande raised the same doubt that resuming without -reindex is already fast on master (mzumsande)
Author agrees the comparison needs real numbers and is investigating before continuing (pinheadmz)

result.summary: Adds persistence of reindex progress (last completed block file plus the in-memory orphan-block map) to the block tree database so an interrupted -reindex can resume instead of restarting from blk00000.dat. On completion the reindex flag and progress keys are erased with a synchronous flush so a crash right after finishing can't force a redundant reindex. The author iterated from writing progress after every file (a performance concern) to writing it only on interrupt.
result.problem: Users who interrupt a long-running -reindex (crash, manual ctrl-c, disk move) currently must redo the entire reindex from the first block file, which can cost hours on large chains. The author hit this personally while moving a node's data directory.

open_concerns: maflcko disputes that the PR provides any real benefit, since correctly restarting without -reindex already resumes quickly by skipping AcceptBlock work on already-indexed files; asks for concrete before/after measurements.
mzumsande separately noted that dropping -reindex on restart already avoids redoing the expensive work, undermining the premise.
Whether the improvement is real depends on the answer to the author's own posed question: does run1+run2 time equal run3 (single uninterrupted reindex)? This is unresolved.
resolved_concerns: Initial concern about slowing the happy path by writing progress after every file was addressed by only persisting progress on interrupt (pinheadmz).

categories.name: indexes
categories.evidence: Changes are entirely within src/node/blockstorage.cpp/.h, the block/undo file storage and BlockTreeDB layer explicitly covered by the indexes category ('block and undo file storage on disk').
categories.rationale: P3 because it targets a real, if narrow, operator pain point: redoing a multi-hour reindex after an interruption, which the author experienced directly ('A few hours in I wanted to change something and hit ctrl-c... I wondered why I had lost those hours of progress'). However a maintainer disputes that the scenario as described actually loses that much work once -reindex is correctly dropped on restart, and no measurements yet substantiate the benefit, so it lacks the clear, uncontested value needed for P2 and is not a correctness or data-integrity issue.

result.card: This draft PR persists reindex progress (last completed block file and the in-memory orphan-block map) to BlockTreeDB so an interrupted -reindex can resume instead of restarting from blk00000.dat, and flushes the reindex-complete flag synchronously to avoid a crash forcing a redundant full reindex. It targets real operator pain: the author lost hours of reindex progress after a manual interrupt. However, maintainer maflcko disputes the premise, arguing that simply dropping -reindex on restart already resumes quickly on current master, and no before/after measurements have been provided to show real benefit; mzumsande echoed the same doubt. The author acknowledged the confusion and moved the PR to draft on 2026-05-08 to gather concrete measurements before continuing, so review right now would likely be invalidated by a rework. No stated dependencies on other PRs, though it overlaps files touched by two other open validation/kernel PRs.
